title: Which OfferCreate flags control passive, immediate-or-cancel, fill-or-kill and sell orders on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced guide to the four order-behaviour flags of an XRPL decentralized-exchange offer, with their hexadecimal values and the cases each one suits.
body:
According to the XRPL OfferCreate reference, four flags change how an order trades: tfPassive, tfImmediateOrCancel, tfFillOrKill and tfSell. Each is a bit set in the Flags field of the OfferCreate transaction. [1]

tfPassive (0x00010000) means the offer does not consume offers that exactly match it, only offers that cross it; this makes it possible to set up offers that peg the exchange rate at a specific value. tfImmediateOrCancel (0x00020000) treats the offer as an Immediate or Cancel order: no Offer entry is placed in the order books, and the transaction trades as much as it can by consuming existing offers when it is processed. [1]

tfFillOrKill (0x00040000) also places no Offer entry in the order books, and it cancels the offer if it cannot be fully filled at the time of execution; by default the owner must receive the full TakerPays amount. tfSell (0x00080000) exchanges the entire TakerGets amount, even if that means obtaining more than the TakerPays amount in exchange. [1]

Author interpretation: use tfFillOrKill when an agent needs all-or-nothing execution, tfImmediateOrCancel when a partial fill is acceptable and nothing should rest on the book, tfPassive for maker-style quotes, and tfSell when the amount sold matters more than the amount received. A submitted OfferCreate is not proof of a trade; read the validated result before treating an order as filled. Sources accessed 11 November 2026. [1]
